results_over_time.note: Paper results, all at 0.0% allowable absolute relative error on OfficeQA Pro (n=133) — paper §2.2 states 'Unless otherwise noted, all results are reported on OfficeQA Pro.' Two groups of rows: (1) Agent baselines from Table 1 — each model paired with its vendor's agent framework (Claude Agent SDK / OpenAI Codex CLI / Gemini CLI); system_description suffix encodes corpus (Full = all bulletins, Oracle = only relevant pages) × format (PDF = raw, DBX Parsed = Databricks-parsed text). Note 'Full corpus' is the document corpus, NOT the OfficeQA-Full 246-question split. (2) LLM baselines from Figure 5 / Appendix E.1 Table 7 — single-call bare-LLM (no agent scaffold), prefixed 'LLM baseline (no agent)'. Prompt Only and Web Search Enabled numbers sourced from Appendix E.1 Table 7 (authoritative numerical table underlying Figure 5); Oracle Pages + Web Search numbers cross-confirmed between Figure 5, Table 7, and page 6 text ('GPT-5.4 improves from 57.1% to 65.4% (+8.3pp), Claude Opus 4.6 from 36.1% to 57.1% (+21.0pp), Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview from 52.6% to 56.4% (+3.8pp)').

results.system_description: zaidishahbaz1/officeqa

results_over_time.note: agentbeats.dev leaderboard, only submission as of 2026-04-20 capture. Evaluated on OfficeQA-Full (n=246 = Pro 133 + Easy 113). Not directly comparable to paper Table 1 (which reports on OfficeQA Pro) — the 113 Easy questions were pre-selected as those the strongest construction-time agents answered correctly, so any system's score on Full is structurally ≥ its score on Pro.

notes: Paper title is 'OfficeQA Pro'; stub name 'OfficeQA' preserved. Pro set is 133 questions; paper also defines OfficeQA Full (Pro + 113 easier questions = 246) for non-frontier systems. Corpus is U.S. Treasury Bulletins (100–200 page reports mixing prose, tables, figures, charts). Capabilities tested: data analysis (56.1%), coding/SQL (15.9%), retrieval (21.8%), chart understanding (5.0%).
